prompt_hint: Join a fact table to a dimension with a RIGHT OUTER JOIN so unmatched right-side rows are retained.
example_snippet: SELECT d.name, s.amt FROM sales s RIGHT OUTER JOIN dim d ON s.dk = d.k
non_degenerate_note: Right side must contain rows with no match; do not add a WHERE filter that makes it inner.

prompt_hint: Combine two tables with a FULL OUTER JOIN keeping unmatched rows from both sides.
example_snippet: SELECT a.k, b.k FROM t_a a FULL OUTER JOIN t_b b ON a.k = b.k
non_degenerate_note: Neither side may be fully covered by the other; avoid predicates that force inner semantics.

prompt_hint: Form a CROSS JOIN (cartesian product) between a small dimension and a computed set.
example_snippet: SELECT a.k, b.g FROM small_a a CROSS JOIN small_b b
non_degenerate_note: Keep both inputs small; do not add an equality predicate (that turns it into an inner join).

prompt_hint: Filter one table to rows whose key appears IN an uncorrelated subquery over another table.
example_snippet: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE cust_k IN (SELECT k FROM customer WHERE region = 'X')
non_degenerate_note: Subquery must be uncorrelated (no reference to the outer query).

prompt_hint: Select rows whose key is NOT IN an uncorrelated subquery to force an anti-semi-join.
example_snippet: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE cust_k NOT IN (SELECT k FROM returns)
non_degenerate_note: Subquery column should be non-nullable to avoid NULL-driven empty results.

prompt_hint: Keep rows for which a correlated EXISTS subquery returns at least one match.
example_snippet: SELECT * FROM customer c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.cust_k = c.k)
non_degenerate_note: Correlation predicate must reference the outer row; may render as SemiJoin or decorrelate.

prompt_hint: Keep rows for which a correlated NOT EXISTS subquery finds no match (anti-join).
example_snippet: SELECT * FROM customer c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.cust_k = c.k)
non_degenerate_note: Correlation predicate must reference the outer row.

prompt_hint: Add a correlated scalar subquery in the SELECT list that aggregates a related table per outer row.
example_snippet: SELECT c.k, (SELECT count(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.cust_k = c.k) AS n FROM customer c
non_degenerate_note: May decorrelate to a Join+Aggregate; keep the correlation to trigger the correlated path.

prompt_hint: Use a LATERAL subquery that references columns from the preceding relation.
example_snippet: SELECT c.k, t.recent FROM customer c CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT max(o.d) AS recent FROM orders o WHERE o.cust_k = c.k) t
non_degenerate_note: LATERAL body must reference the outer relation.

prompt_hint: Compare a column against an uncorrelated scalar subquery that returns exactly one row.
example_snippet: SELECT * FROM item WHERE price > (SELECT avg(price) FROM item)
non_degenerate_note: Subquery must return a single row (aggregate or LIMIT 1).

prompt_hint: Aggregate over multiple GROUPING SETS in one query.
example_snippet: SELECT a, b, sum(v) FROM t GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((a,b),(a),())
non_degenerate_note: Use at least two distinct grouping sets.

prompt_hint: Produce subtotals and a grand total with GROUP BY ROLLUP.
example_snippet: SELECT a, b, sum(v) FROM t GROUP BY ROLLUP (a, b)
non_degenerate_note: Use two or more columns so the rollup has intermediate levels.

prompt_hint: Compute all-dimension combinations with GROUP BY CUBE.
example_snippet: SELECT a, b, sum(v) FROM t GROUP BY CUBE (a, b)
non_degenerate_note: Use two or more columns.

prompt_hint: Compute two or more DISTINCT aggregates on different columns in one query.
example_snippet: SELECT count(DISTINCT a), count(DISTINCT b) FROM t
non_degenerate_note: Distinct columns must differ; strategy (MarkDistinct vs subqueries) is stats-chosen.

prompt_hint: Add a ranking window function partitioned and ordered over a table.
example_snippet: SELECT k, rank() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY v DESC) AS r FROM t
non_degenerate_note: Do NOT filter on the rank result (that would convert to TopNRanking).

prompt_hint: Add an analytic window function such as LAG, LEAD, or a running SUM over an ordered partition.
example_snippet: SELECT k, sum(v) OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY d ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS rt FROM t
non_degenerate_note: Include PARTITION BY and ORDER BY to force a real Window operator.

prompt_hint: Return the top-k rows per group using a ranking window function filtered to rank<=k.
example_snippet: SELECT * FROM (SELECT k, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY v DESC) rn FROM t) WHERE rn <= 5
non_degenerate_note: The rank<=k filter is what triggers TopNRanking; keep k small and constant.

prompt_hint: Assign a global or partitioned ROW_NUMBER without any downstream rank filter.
example_snippet: SELECT k, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY v) AS rn FROM t
non_degenerate_note: Must not be followed by a rn<=k filter (that yields TopNRanking instead).

prompt_hint: Intersect the key sets of two subqueries with INTERSECT.
example_snippet: SELECT k FROM t_a INTERSECT SELECT k FROM t_b
non_degenerate_note: Both sides must project the same column set.

prompt_hint: Subtract one key set from another with EXCEPT.
example_snippet: SELECT k FROM t_a EXCEPT SELECT k FROM t_b
non_degenerate_note: Both sides must project the same column set.

prompt_hint: Combine two selects with UNION (distinct) to force a dedup aggregate over the union.
example_snippet: SELECT k, v FROM t_a UNION SELECT k, v FROM t_b
non_degenerate_note: Use UNION not UNION ALL so a distinct aggregate is added.

prompt_hint: Expand an array or map column with UNNEST joined to its parent row.
example_snippet: SELECT t.k, u.e FROM t CROSS JOIN UNNEST(t.arr) AS u(e)
non_degenerate_note: Requires an array/map-typed column in the schema.

prompt_hint: Sample a fraction of a table with TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI.
example_snippet: SELECT * FROM big_table TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (10)
non_degenerate_note: Apply to a base table reference; percentage between 0 and 100.

prompt_hint: Page results with ORDER BY combined with OFFSET and FETCH/LIMIT.
example_snippet: SELECT k FROM t ORDER BY v OFFSET 20 LIMIT 10
non_degenerate_note: OFFSET must be non-zero to retain the Offset operator.

prompt_hint: Traverse a hierarchy with a WITH RECURSIVE CTE (anchor UNION ALL recursive step).
example_snippet: WITH RECURSIVE r(k, lvl) AS (SELECT k, 0 FROM node WHERE parent IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT n.k, r.lvl+1 FROM node n JOIN r ON n.parent = r.k) SELECT * FROM r
non_degenerate_note: Requires a self-referential parent/child relationship; bound recursion depth.

prompt_hint: Return the top rows by an ordering expression with ORDER BY plus LIMIT.
example_snippet: SELECT k, v FROM t ORDER BY v DESC LIMIT 20
non_degenerate_note: ORDER BY and LIMIT together always merge into TopN.
